questions.question_text: Which decimal number of metres is equivalent to $176$ cm?

options.why: Treated ten centimetres as one metre instead of one hundred.
Treated one thousand centimetres as one metre.
Placed all remaining centimetres into thousandths of a metre.

questions.question_text: How should $4.38$ m be recorded using metres and centimetres?

options.why: Treated the decimal digits as three centimetres and eight millimetres instead of thirty-eight centimetres.
Ignored the tenths digit, which represents thirty centimetres.
Moved the tenths digit into the whole-metre part.

questions.question_text: Which decimal number of centimetres is equivalent to $93$ mm?

options.why: Divided by one hundred instead of ten millimetres per centimetre.
Changed the unit label without changing the numerical value.
Placed the tens digit into whole centimetres without regrouping.

questions.question_text: How should $21.4$ cm be recorded using centimetres and millimetres?

options.why: Treated four tenths of a centimetre as forty millimetres.
Split the written digits without using decimal place value.
Kept the decimal unchanged when moving to the smaller unit.

questions.question_text: Write $7$ m $6$ cm using metres in decimal notation.

options.why: Placed six centimetres in the tenths place instead of the hundredths place.
Treated centimetres as thousandths of a metre.
Added the numbers seven and six as though both were whole metres.

questions.question_text: Which mixed-unit length is equivalent to $5.082$ m?

options.why: Read eighty-two millimetres as eighty-two centimetres.
Swapped the hundredths and thousandths unit meanings.
Treated the hundredths digit as eighty centimetres rather than eight.

questions.solution_text:
$0.082\text{ m}=82\text{ mm}$
$82\text{ mm}=8\text{ cm }2\text{ mm}$
$5.082\text{ m}=5\text{ m }8\text{ cm }2\text{ mm}$
